info.title: Forma runtime API: the whatsapp client
info.description:
A Forma runtime serves one agent (or, multi-tenant, every deployed agent) to one kind of client, which its runtime file names (`client:`). The paths are the same for every client; what they take and return is not. This describes one client.

**`client: whatsapp`**: the agent as the webhook of a WhatsApp Cloud API app. Meta calls it, and the agent answers over WhatsApp: nothing of yours calls it. It always keeps conversations, and needs no API key: every delivery is signed by Meta.

get.description:
Meta calls it when the webhook's URL or verify token is set in the
App Dashboard. If the token is the server's, the server answers with
the challenge, and Meta starts delivering messages.

parameters.name: hub.verify_token
parameters.description:
The verify token chosen in Meta's App Dashboard: the server's
`WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN` (or the deployment's `verify_token`).

parameters.name: X-Deployment-ID
parameters.description: Multi-tenant servers only: the deployment the webhook is for. Your reverse proxy adds it, from the URL it gave Meta for that deployment.

200.description: The challenge, as it was sent

400.description: `hub.mode` is not `subscribe`, a query parameter is missing, or the server has no WhatsApp credentials

401.description: The verify token is not the server's

post.summary: Receives what WhatsApp delivers (Meta calls it).
post.description:
Every delivery must be signed by Meta with the App secret
(`X-Hub-Signature-256`), or it is refused. Messages (text, pictures,
voice notes, documents) are answered over WhatsApp: each sender has
one conversation with the agent, whose id is their phone number.
Reactions are stored on the message they react to; statuses are
acknowledged. A message Meta delivers again is answered once, and one
that arrives while the agent still answers the sender waits its turn.

Calls that need an approval are asked with two buttons; delegated
tools are answered at once, with an error (there is no client to run
them). The answer to Meta is what the deliveries' jobs consumed.

parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
parameters.description: `sha256=` and the HMAC-SHA256 of the body, with the App secret (`WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET`, or the deployment's `app_secret`). Meta adds it.

parameters.name: X-Deployment-ID
parameters.description: Multi-tenant servers only: the deployment the webhook is for. Your reverse proxy adds it, from the URL it gave Meta for that deployment, and passes the body and Meta's headers on unchanged.

requestBody.description: A [WhatsApp Cloud API webhook payload](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/overview/), as Meta sends it.

200.description: The delivery was handled (or ignored: another number's, or a kind the agent does not handle). What answering it consumed, one entry per job.

400.description: The body is not a WhatsApp delivery, or the server has no WhatsApp credentials

401.description: The signature is missing, malformed, or wrong

409.description: The agent was still answering the sender's previous message after a while: Meta delivers it again later

500.description: The message could not be stored or answered, and delivering it again may help

calls.description: Provider round trips, which some plans bill per-request on top of tokens.

model.description: The model the provider reports having served.

provider.description:
The backend that served the calls, by its OpenTelemetry GenAI name
(`ollama`, `openai`, `groq`, `gcp.vertex_ai`).

server_address.description:
The host the calls went to (OpenTelemetry's `server.address`): with
`provider`, who served them, and so who bills them. Every
OpenAI-compatible server speaks `openai`; the host tells them apart.

ModelUsage.description:
What one `(provider, server_address, model)` consumed across a whole run.

Provider is half the key, not decoration: the same model name reached
through two backends is two different prices, and through a local Ollama it
is free.

TokenUsage.description:
What one LLM call consumed, in the shape a bill needs.

This is a *normalisation* of [`OpenAIUsage`], not a copy of it. Providers
disagree about what their totals include, and the disagreement shows up as
a wrong invoice rather than a parse error, so the convention is pinned here,
once, at the only layer that still knows which provider produced the numbers:

- `input_tokens` counts every prompt token, `cached_input_tokens` included.
- `output_tokens` counts every generated token, `reasoning_tokens` included.

`cached_input_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens` are therefore *subsets* of their
parents, carried separately because they are priced differently — cached
input is discounted, reasoning is billed at the output rate. Adding either to
its parent double-charges.

cached_input_tokens.description:
The subset of `input_tokens` the provider served from its prompt cache.
Billed at a discount, so ignoring it over-charges.

input_audio_tokens.description:
Audio tokens in the prompt, a subset of `input_tokens`. Priced far above
text tokens by every provider that supports them.

output_audio_tokens.description: Audio tokens generated, a subset of `output_tokens`.

reasoning_tokens.description:
The subset of `output_tokens` spent on reasoning the client never sees.
Billed like any other output token.

ToolUsage.description:
What a tool consumed beyond being called, in a unit it is priced by: the
seconds a code-execution sandbox ran, for instance. Summed per
`(tool_kind, unit)` across a run.

quantity.description: How many `unit`s, over the whole job.

UsageTally.description:
Groups [`SSEvent::Usage`] events by `(provider, server_address, model)`, lists the kind of
every tool called ([`SSEvent::ToolInputAvailable`]), and sums
[`SSEvent::ToolUsage`] by kind and unit.

tokens.description:
What each provider and model consumed, one entry per pair.

Insertion-ordered so a run's first model leads the report, which makes
logs and fixtures stable to read.

tool_usage.description: What tools consumed in units of their own (absent when nothing).

tools.description: The kind of every tool called, once per call.
